items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

ctx.x: Okay. Yeah because that was a sort of a — I don’t know if I would call it a down time for pop music but there wasn’t anything really strong for a number of years there so I think your timing was pretty good for that.

Some people who are historians and know about this stuff really think that Elvis was a watershed. And some very fine musicians believe that, you know, he wasn’t just a kind of a great pop guy, I mean he really made a huge difference in how we all thought about and listened to music. Leonard Bernstein said that.

I’ve had a number of musicians say that. Yeah, that that was a big transition from swing to straight-eighth notes is how some of the musicians would characterize it. That’s terrific. And your parents thought this was a pretty good way for you to make a buck?
